controls: Keep the numerical algorithm and constant bit patterns byte-identical; hoisting must not change FMA order or values.
Enumerate the FP/GPR register budget with the host kernel contract so hoisted constants are not clobbered by other injector ops (v_aux/vmm_mask/v0 usage) and no spills are introduced.
Limit the hoist to constants that are provably loop-invariant and never written inside the loop; re-derive the register contract for exp/erf/log/tanh/gelu paths that share the injector.
Keep the raw Xbyak_riscv vf-form emission style unchanged so only the materialization site moves.
reasons: The injector is shared by many eltwise algorithms and the host kernel, so a change to FP register allocation risks clobbering live values and introducing spills.
FP constants are used as vf-form scalar operands; a hoist changes live ranges and must not extend them into spills at LMUL=1 or higher.
If the loop is latency-bound on the FMA dependency chain rather than issue-bound, hoisting reduces instruction count but may yield a smaller speedup than the instruction-share estimate suggests.

conditions.description: The change targets the rv64 eltwise JIT injector code emission, not the numerical algorithm.
benchdnn eltwise_f16_upstream on SG2044/C920v2 remains the measurement workload.
The JIT host kernel (jit_uni_kernel) retains the strip-mined loop shape and per-chunk vsetvli.

actions.proposal: In the rv64 eltwise JIT injector (src/cpu/rv64/injectors/jit_uni_eltwise_injector.cpp), change the constant-emission contract so the ~25 loop-invariant f32 constants (MINLOGF, MAXLOGF, log2e, C1, C2, exp-poly p0..p5, erf/erf-related coefficients, 0.5/1.0/2.0, mask 0x7fffffff, shifts 126/23) are hoisted out of the per-iteration loop body: materialize each constant once in a loop prologue into dedicated FP scalar registers (or load once from a small rodata constant table) and have the in-loop vf-form ops reference those pre-loaded registers instead of calling load_f32_const at each use site. This requires the injector to expose a hoist/prologue step or to split constant setup from per-element compute so the emitter does not re-emit li+fmv_w_x per iteration.

correctness_checks: Run benchdnn eltwise eltwise_f16_upstream (and the exp/log/tanh/gelu/erf eltwise cases that share the injector) and confirm results match the reference within the benchdnn tolerance used by the test.

Dump the JIT buffer (objdump or jit dump) and verify each f32 constant appears materialized exactly once before the loop and the loop body no longer contains lui/addiw/fmv.w.x sequences for those constants.
Verify no new FP-register spills or save/restore appear in the generated kernel around the loop.
Verify the emitted instruction count of the loop body decreases by roughly the number of hoisted constant-setup instructions (target ~60-70 fewer per iteration).

expected_signals.signal: perf stat instruction count for the workload drops by ~30-50% if the kernel dominates, or equivalently the generated loop body shrinks by ~60-70 instructions per iteration.
perf annotate samples on the lui/addiw/fmv.w.x addresses (0xa4-0x29c) disappear or collapse to a single prologue cluster before the loop.
benchdnn_min_ms / avg_ms for eltwise_f16_upstream decrease measurably (issue-bound expectation).
IPC rises toward the FP-issue ceiling if the loop was issue-bound on constant materialization.
Any new FP-register live-range conflict, clobber of a host-held constant by another injector op, or register spill appears in the generated code.
Any numerical mismatch in exp/erf/log/tanh eltwise results appears if a constant value or FMA order changed.

success_criteria: Generated loop body instruction count drops by ~60-70 instructions per iteration (objdump of JIT buffer).
benchdnn eltwise_f16_upstream min_ms decreases by a measurable margin (>=5% target; issue-bound expectation is larger).
No numerical regression across the shared-injector eltwise algorithms (benchdnn correctness passes).
No new register spills or save/restore in the generated kernel.

controls: Never assume m8; enumerate and benchmark each legal candidate on the target before selecting.
Keep fractional-LMUL widening legal (f16 m2 -> f32 m2) and avoid introducing vlmul_ext/trunc or conversions.
Preserve tail handling and mask/tail semantics for the remainder chunk.
Regenerate the register-live-set budget for the eltwise injector's v_aux/v_mask usage at each candidate LMUL.
reasons: Larger LMUL can be slower if the budget is exceeded and vectors spill, or if the loop is latency-bound on the FMA dependency chain rather than issue-bound.
Widening f16->f32 changes EMUL relationships and could force fractional-LMUL or conversion overhead that cancels the amortization gain.
The LMUL in the current kernel is inferred (vsetvli opcode is not decoded by the available objdump), so the baseline LMUL and live set must be confirmed by disassembly first.

conditions.description: The change is evaluated on the same SG2044/C920v2 (VLEN=128) workload after constant hoisting.
The JIT host kernel can supply a different vtype/LMUL to the eltwise injector without changing the eltwise math.
f16 input elements are processed with legal f16->f32 widening EMUL ratios.

actions.proposal: After (or independently of) hoisting loop-invariant constants, evaluate raising the RVV LMUL of the eltwise compute from m1 to m2/m4 in the rv64 JIT kernel so each iteration processes 16/32 f16 lanes on VLEN=128, amortizing the fixed per-iteration vsetvli, pointer update, and branch cost over more elements. Select only spill-free candidates that satisfy LMUL*peak_live_vectors<=32 with legal f16->f32 widening EMUL, and retain strip-mined tails.

correctness_checks: Enumerate legal m1/m2/m4 candidates and verify LMUL*peak_live_vectors<=32 including v_aux0/v_aux1/v_aux2, mask v0, source/dest, and widening EMUL.
Inspect the generated JIT code for each candidate to confirm no vlmul_ext/vlmul_trunc, no vector spills, and group alignment holds.
Run benchdnn eltwise f16 upstream for m1/m2/m4 and confirm element-by-element results match the m1 baseline within tolerance (LMUL must not change lane values).
Cover short/medium/long input lengths including tail chunks across VLEN=128.

expected_signals.signal: perf annotate shows fewer vsetvli / pointer-update / back-branch instructions per element as elements per iteration double or quadruple.
benchdnn_min_ms decreases if the loop was amortization-bound after constant hoisting.
Elements processed per iteration (VLMAX) increases to 16/32 for f16 lanes.
Vector spills, vlmul_ext/vlmul_trunc, or stack slots appear in the generated code at m2/m4, indicating the budget was exceeded and the candidate must step down.
Numerical mismatches appear if widening EMUL or tail/mask handling changes lane semantics.

success_criteria: At least one legal spill-free m2/m4 candidate is generated and benchmarked.
benchdnn eltwise_f16_upstream min_ms improves versus the m1 baseline at the selected LMUL.
No vector spills, vlmul_ext/vlmul_trunc, or conversions are introduced in the generated code.
Numerical results remain within tolerance across m1/m2/m4 and across input lengths including tails.

review_items.description: Re-disassemble the JIT buffer with an RVV-aware objdump/llvm-objdump or use the Xbyak_riscv emitter dump to confirm the exact vtype (SEW/LMUL) and opcode mix in jit_uni_kernel.2.

Collect a per-function or generated-blob instruction/cycle attribution (e.g., perf record on jitted-*.so symbols) and an A/B of benchdnn_min_ms before/after the emitter change to bound the real benefit.
Locate the rv64 eltwise kernel that embeds the injector loop (search jit_uni_eltwise / eltwise_utils in src/cpu/rv64) to confirm where a constant-hoisting prologue can be emitted.

alternative_explanations.explanation: The intrinsic exp/erf polynomial FMA chain is not free: single compute lines (0x14c 4.24%, 0x150 3.64%) carry the largest per-line shares. But the ~70 constant-setup instructions per iteration outnumber the ~45 RVV compute ops, and their lines are consistently sampled, so constant hoisting remains the dominant lever.

With VLEN=128 and only 8 f16 lanes per iteration at LMUL=1, fixed loop cost is under-amortized; however raising LMUL alone does not remove constant-setup instructions, which are proportional to the number of vf-form ops and unchanged by LMUL, so constant hoisting is needed regardless.

The `.insn 4, 0x...` lines are valid RVV encodings emitted by the Xbyak_riscv backend (cpu_isa_traits.hpp sets XBYAK_RISCV_V=1); the toolchain objdump lacks RVV decode support, so this is a display artifact, not miscompiled code.

findings.conclusion: In the JIT-emitted RVV eltwise kernel jit_uni_kernel.2, the rv64 eltwise JIT injector re-materializes ~25 loop-invariant f32 constants inside the hot loop on every iteration (lui+addiw+fmv.w.x and li sequences at 0xa4-0x29c), which is ~70 of ~135 loop instructions (~52%); the emitter's load_f32_const places li+fmv_w_x at each use site instead of hoisting constants before the loop or loading them from a constant table, and this redundant per-iteration materialization is the dominant instruction-issue cost of the measured hotspot.

neighbor_exclusions.reason: The lui+addiw+fmv.w.x sequences are already the minimal form for loading these f32 constants into FP registers for vf-form ops; the defect is loop-invariant repetition across iterations, which is an emitter hoisting/quality issue, not a shorter-ALU-sequence issue.
No stack spills or save/restore are evidenced in the JIT loop; the root cause is redundant constant emission by the emitter contract, not register allocation pressure.

findings.reasoning: Disassembly of jit_uni_kernel.2 shows the hot loop body 0x8c-0x2c0 contains ~27 lui + ~18 addiw + ~25 fmv.w.x + 2 li sequences re-materializing the identical f32 constants (MINLOGF/MAXLOGF/log2e/C1/C2/exp-poly and erf-poly coefficients, mask 0x7fffffff, shift 126/23) on every iteration. The source load_f32_const (jit_uni_eltwise_injector.cpp:81) emits li+fmv_w_x at each use site inside the loop, and exp/erf/log paths call it per constant. Constant setup is ~70 of ~135 loop instructions (~52%), with hotspot lines spread across both constant loads and RVV ops; IPC 0.679 and low cache/branch miss rates indicate an issue-bound compute loop. Hoisting constants out of the loop or loading them from a constant pool would remove roughly half the loop instructions.

alternative_explanations.explanation: The eltwise kernel uses v_aux0/v_aux1/v_aux2 plus mask v0 and source/destination vectors, so the register budget at m2/m4 must be enumerated (LMUL*peak_live<=32) before any LMUL raise; widening f16->f32 also adds EMUL constraints.

Constant setup is proportional to the number of vf-form ops, which is unchanged by LMUL, so LMUL alone cannot remove the constant-materialization overhead; this is why constant hoisting is the primary fix and LMUL tuning is complementary.

IPC 0.679 could indicate the FMA dependency chain latency bounds the loop; larger LMUL does not shorten the polynomial dependency chain, only amortizes bookkeeping, so the benefit depends on whether the loop is issue- or latency-bound.

findings.conclusion: With VLEN=128 and f16 lanes (pointer advance slli t1,t0,1 in the loop tail), each iteration of jit_uni_kernel.2 processes at most 8 f16 elements at LMUL=1, so the fixed per-iteration cost (vsetvli, pointer updates, back branch, and all constant setup) is amortized over very few elements (~135 instructions per 8-element chunk); raising LMUL to m2/m4 would amortize the same fixed loop cost over 16/32 lanes per iteration, subject to the spill-free register budget.

neighbor_exclusions.reason: The per-iteration vsetvli is required for strip-mining over the remaining count a4 (the vl is not loop-invariant until the main-loop/tail split), so it is not redundant vector-state bookkeeping.
The kernel already uses direct vf-form ops consuming FP scalar registers; no redundant vfmv.v.f broadcast temporary of a scalar constant is evidenced.

findings.reasoning: Metadata fixes VLEN=128 on C920v2; the loop advances pointers by t0*2 bytes (slli t1,t0,1) so each iteration processes t0 f16 elements, at most 8 with LMUL=1. The loop body is ~135 instructions for 8 elements (~17 instructions/element), a very high per-element cost that includes vsetvli (0x90), pointer updates, the back branch, and all constant setup. Raising LMUL to m2/m4 would amortize the fixed per-iteration vsetvli/pointer/branch cost over 16/32 lanes, but the LMUL is inferred (vsetvli opcode is not decoded by this objdump), so this is a contributing factor with medium confidence.

alternative_explanations.explanation: The RVV encodings are emitted by the Xbyak_riscv JIT backend used across the rv64 GEMM/brgemm/injector code (src/cpu/rv64); the toolchain objdump used for perf annotate simply lacks RVV disassembly support, so the raw `.insn` display carries no signal of broken code.

findings.conclusion: The `.insn 4, 0x...` entries throughout jit_uni_kernel.2 are undecodable-by-this-objdump RVV instructions emitted by the Xbyak_riscv JIT backend, not corrupted or miscompiled code; they should not be treated as evidence of a codegen bug.
findings.reasoning: The entire rv64 backend emits raw RVV encodings via Xbyak_riscv (cpu_isa_traits.hpp: XBYAK_RISCV_V=1), and the disassembler in the perf environment renders them as `.insn 4, 0x...`. The injector source confirms the intended sequence (vsetvli, vle/vse, vf-form FMA/mul/add, vmerge) matches the observed constant pattern, so the `.insn` lines are a tooling artifact, not a defect.

asm.reason: Hotspot is JIT-generated RVV code (jitted-12109-2.so) emitted via Xbyak_riscv from jit_uni_eltwise_injector.cpp; no handwritten .S kernel for rv64 eltwise is evidenced. No policy-backed missing-S or handwritten-asm signal.

codegen.reason: JIT-generated code shows repeated in-loop lui/addiw/fmv.w.x constant materialization triples (~20+ constants) plus integer li for shift/mask constants inside the hot loop; instruction shape and data-movement overhead evidenced across hotspot lines 0x100-0x2ac.

crypto.reason: No cryptographic arithmetic, cipher, hash, checksum, or binary-field work; target is an eltwise transcendental polynomial kernel.

offload.reason: No packed-SIMD, matrix-engine, or parallel GEMM offload opportunity for an elementwise activation kernel; already RVV vectorized in-loop.

operator_rvv.reason: Kernel is already lane-parallel RVV (vfmacc/vfmul/vfadd etc.), not a scalar operator awaiting an RVV formulation; the lane-independent formulation is already in place.

runtime_os.reason: No timer, interrupt, privileged-boundary, or runtime context management in the measured function; pure compute loop with branch back-edge.

string_memory.reason: Not string/memory/checksum work; L1 miss rate 0.328% and branch miss 0.360% show no memory or branch-pattern domination, L1_dcache_loads 160.9M vs misses 527K.

vectorized_tuning.reason: Existing JIT-generated RVV loop re-executes vsetvli (0x90) and re-materializes loop-invariant FP constants and integer bookkeeping (li 126/23/0x7fffffff) on every iteration; vector configuration and bookkeeping overhead is the evident bottleneck shape.
